story.headline: Microsoft signed school AI privacy terms. Schools must request the protections.

heroVisual.alt: An illustrated school desk with a tablet, exercise books and a paper form.

story.the_story:
Microsoft and the American Federation of Teachers signed a school AI safety and privacy agreement on September 7 and announced it with the United Federation of Teachers on September 9. US school districts can incorporate the protections into their Microsoft agreements, making them contractually enforceable.

The scope matters. Schools must opt in, and the agreement covers primarily education-designed generative AI: software that creates text or other content from instructions. General productivity, communications, search and workplace-assistance products are excluded, even when a school licenses them.
story.laidies_read:
The agreement prohibits using covered student and educator information for training—changing an AI model for future use—with a narrow safety and security exception. That exception cannot feed general model improvement, advertising or unrelated commercial uses. It also bans companion features designed to create attachment or keep students engaged beyond the learning task.

There is a separate category called telemetry: anonymous technical records about how a service operates. Those records may support reliability and product improvements, but not generative-model training or individual student profiling. “No training” does not mean “no data processing.”

Nor does a privacy agreement certify a good lesson. Associated Press reports that Fairplay’s Josh Golin welcomed meaningful protections but warned they leave unanswered whether classroom AI is appropriate, and at what age. AP also reports that OpenAI and Anthropic are discussing their own agreements; Google has not said whether it will offer similar protections. This is not an industry-wide settlement.
story.what_this_means:
Imagine a child is assigned an AI tutor. Ask which exact product is being assigned and whether the school incorporated these standards into its agreement. A general work assistant used by a teacher is not covered simply because Microsoft supplies it.

The agreement requires notices that AI answers may be incorrect. Privacy protection does not establish learning value.
story.cocktail_party: “Request school-specific terms for covered education AI. Privacy commitments do not guarantee correct answers.”
story.class_notes: AI Fundamentals 101: Testing and Evaluation explains why the question an evaluation tests matters. Privacy protection and learning value require different evidence.

legal-policy.legalStatus: Signed contractual standard; US school districts may incorporate applicable protections into customer agreements.

legal-policy.unresolvedQuestions: Specific school implementation, output accuracy, educational appropriateness and other vendor signatures remain open.
